Two more native structures round out control flow:

- **`WHILE`** repeats while a condition holds. **`BREAK`** exits a loop early;
  **`CONTINUE`** skips to the next iteration.
- **`TRY` / `EXCEPT`** catches a failing keyword and handles it, instead of
  failing the test. Optional `ELSE` and `FINALLY` blocks round it out.

Both close with `END`.

## Task 1 — Write a WHILE loop with BREAK and a TRY/EXCEPT

**Goal:** create `checks/robust.robot` with a `WHILE` loop that stops early with
`BREAK`, and a test that catches a failing keyword with `TRY` / `EXCEPT`.

Here is the same pair over different numbers and messages. Adapt them.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Test Cases ***
Counts To Five
    ${n}=    Set Variable    ${0}
    WHILE    ${n} < 100
        ${n}=    Evaluate    ${n} + 1
        IF    ${n} == 5    BREAK
    END
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${n}    5

Recovers From An Error
    TRY
        Fail    kaboom
    EXCEPT    kaboom
        Log    recovered
    END
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** `checks/robust.robot` uses `WHILE` and `TRY`, and `While With Break`
passes.

<!-- hint -->
Start a counter at `${0}`, loop with `WHILE    ${i} < 10`, increment inside with
`Evaluate`, and `IF    ${i} == 3    BREAK`. Close with `END`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
Wrap a failing keyword: `TRY`, then `Fail    boom`, then `EXCEPT    boom`, then
`Log    handled`, then `END`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Test Cases ***
While With Break
    ${i}=    Set Variable    ${0}
    WHILE    ${i} < 10
        ${i}=    Evaluate    ${i} + 1
        IF    ${i} == 3    BREAK
    END
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${i}    3

Try Except Handles Failure
    TRY
        Fail    boom
    EXCEPT    boom
        Log    handled
    END
```
<!-- /solution -->
